neighbours.label: temporal anchoring of an event or habit: 'That night,', weekday dates, 'daily', habitual 'would/always'
fire: The storm knocked out the power grid. That night, the whole town lit candles.
Our book club meets on Tuesday, March 4, at the public library.
The museum opens its new wing Friday, with a ribbon cutting at noon.
She left for college in August. That evening, her parents sat in silence.
The farmers market runs from May to October, daily between 8 a.m. and noon.
After the funeral, my grandfather would sit on the porch for hours.
The team lost on Saturday, then won the rematch at home on Monday.
Every summer I always keep a spare key under the flowerpot by the door.
quiet: The storm knocked out the power grid. The whole town lit candles in the dark.
Our book club meets in the reading room at the public library.
The museum opens its new wing with a ribbon cutting by the mayor.
She left for college in Boston. Her parents sat in silence in the kitchen.
The farmers market sells honey, apples and fresh bread from local growers.
After the funeral, my grandfather sat on the porch with his old dog.
The team lost to the visitors, then won the rematch at home by two goals.
My neighbor keeps a spare key under the flowerpot by the door.

notes: Card: 'That night', 'Sunday, October 23,', 'Saturday,', 'daily', 'He would', 'I always'. Logit effect of + pole promotes days/weeks/weekly, so the - pole likely marks when-an-event-happens framing. Broad pole (1.1%).
